rows.text: The characteristic curve relates engine torque output to engine speed, not vehicle weight.
evidence: Robert Bosch GmbH, Gasoline-engine management: Basics and components, p. 7, “Power output and torque”, fig. 1, https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1539828/download-documents?artifactId=UJEpDOFJ-6vQkdEVveZ9_ls3MAYETAk160ZIPyF9DS8uYS08NL8ygDY: typical manifold-injection gasoline engine curves plot torque and power against rpm; torque rises to a maximum and falls; power rises to a maximum and then falls in the figure, at a higher rpm than peak torque.

rows.text: In a typical characteristic curve, torque rises with engine speed to a maximum and then falls; it does not follow the stated minimum.
evidence: Robert Bosch GmbH, Gasoline-engine management: Basics and components, p. 7, “Power output and torque”, fig. 1, https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1539828/download-documents?artifactId=UJEpDOFJ-6vQkdEVveZ9_ls3MAYETAk160ZIPyF9DS8uYS08NL8ygDY: typical manifold-injection gasoline engine curves plot torque and power against rpm; torque rises to a maximum and falls; power rises to a maximum and then falls in the figure, at a higher rpm than peak torque.

rows.text: Torque is the product of the force and its perpendicular lever arm about the axis, not their sum.
evidence: https://openstax.org/books/physics/pages/6-3-rotational-motion, sezione Torque: τ = rF sin θ.

rows.text: The power curve shows power output at different engine speeds, not torque against vehicle dimensions.
evidence: Robert Bosch GmbH, Gasoline-engine management: Basics and components, p. 7, “Power output and torque”, fig. 1, https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1539828/download-documents?artifactId=UJEpDOFJ-6vQkdEVveZ9_ls3MAYETAk160ZIPyF9DS8uYS08NL8ygDY: typical manifold-injection gasoline engine curves plot torque and power against rpm; torque rises to a maximum and falls; power rises to a maximum and then falls in the figure, at a higher rpm than peak torque.

rows.text: On a typical characteristic curve, power rises with engine speed to a maximum and then falls; the exact point depends on the engine.
evidence: Robert Bosch GmbH, Gasoline-engine management: Basics and components, p. 7, “Power output and torque”, fig. 1, https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1539828/download-documents?artifactId=UJEpDOFJ-6vQkdEVveZ9_ls3MAYETAk160ZIPyF9DS8uYS08NL8ygDY: typical manifold-injection gasoline engine curves plot torque and power against rpm; torque rises to a maximum and falls; power rises to a maximum and then falls in the figure, at a higher rpm than peak torque.

rows.text: The curve lets you compare the power available at different engine speeds.
evidence: Robert Bosch GmbH, Gasoline-engine management: Basics and components, p. 7, “Power output and torque”, fig. 1, https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1539828/download-documents?artifactId=UJEpDOFJ-6vQkdEVveZ9_ls3MAYETAk160ZIPyF9DS8uYS08NL8ygDY: typical manifold-injection gasoline engine curves plot torque and power against rpm; torque rises to a maximum and falls; power rises to a maximum and then falls in the figure, at a higher rpm than peak torque.

rows.text: The quiz marks this FALSE. The torque curve alone cannot identify maximum fuel consumption: at the same engine speed, consumption also changes with load. Comparing consumption requires the engine map and a specified measurement.
evidence: US DOE Co-Optima webinar https://www.energy.gov/cmei/fuels/text-version-co-optima-webinar-how-can-co-optimized-fuels-and-spark-ignition-engines — efficiency map depends on speed and load, with light-duty spark-ignition research examples. It does not establish the quiz’s claimed coincidence for an unspecified engine/load or a model-specific near-peak optimum.

NREL vehicle choice and applied analysis https://www.energy.gov/cmei/vehicles/articles/medium-and-heavy-duty-vehicle-choice-modeling-and-applied-analysis — fuel-rate maps relate operation to speed and torque; distinguish fuel rate from efficiency. Printed answer retained without asserting a demonstrated near-peak efficiency optimum.

rows.text: The typical power curve rises to a maximum and then falls; it does not first reach a minimum as stated.
evidence: Robert Bosch GmbH, Gasoline-engine management: Basics and components, p. 7, “Power output and torque”, fig. 1, https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1539828/download-documents?artifactId=UJEpDOFJ-6vQkdEVveZ9_ls3MAYETAk160ZIPyF9DS8uYS08NL8ygDY: typical manifold-injection gasoline engine curves plot torque and power against rpm; torque rises to a maximum and falls; power rises to a maximum and then falls in the figure, at a higher rpm than peak torque.

It does not establish the quiz’s claimed coincidence for an unspecified engine/load or a model-specific near-peak optimum.

rows.text: On a typical characteristic curve, torque rises to a maximum and then decreases at higher engine speeds.
evidence: Robert Bosch GmbH, Gasoline-engine management: Basics and components, p. 7, “Power output and torque”, fig. 1, https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1539828/download-documents?artifactId=UJEpDOFJ-6vQkdEVveZ9_ls3MAYETAk160ZIPyF9DS8uYS08NL8ygDY: typical manifold-injection gasoline engine curves plot torque and power against rpm; torque rises to a maximum and falls; power rises to a maximum and then falls in the figure, at a higher rpm than peak torque.

rows.text: The two peaks do not necessarily coincide: power depends on both torque and rotational speed and can continue rising after peak torque.
evidence: Robert Bosch GmbH, Gasoline-engine management: Basics and components, p. 7, “Power output and torque”, fig. 1, https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1539828/download-documents?artifactId=UJEpDOFJ-6vQkdEVveZ9_ls3MAYETAk160ZIPyF9DS8uYS08NL8ygDY: typical manifold-injection gasoline engine curves plot torque and power against rpm; torque rises to a maximum and falls; power rises to a maximum and then falls in the figure, at a higher rpm than peak torque.

OpenStax, University Physics Vol. 1, §10.8, https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/10-8-work-and-power-for-rotational-motion: rotational power equals torque times angular velocity.

rows.text: The curves show how available torque and power change with engine speed, describing useful engine characteristics.
evidence: Robert Bosch GmbH, Gasoline-engine management: Basics and components, p. 7, “Power output and torque”, fig. 1, https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1539828/download-documents?artifactId=UJEpDOFJ-6vQkdEVveZ9_ls3MAYETAk160ZIPyF9DS8uYS08NL8ygDY: typical manifold-injection gasoline engine curves plot torque and power against rpm; torque rises to a maximum and falls; power rises to a maximum and then falls in the figure, at a higher rpm than peak torque.

rows.text: Keeping the engine at maximum speed all the time is not a rule for reducing emissions. Efficient driving uses a gear and engine speed suited to conditions.
evidence: UK Department for Transport, Efficient Driving: A Rapid Evidence Assessment, pp. 65–66, https://www.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/509972/efficient-driving-rapid-evidence-assessment.pdf: reported 2,000 versus 3,000 rpm upshifts reduced NO in one older study but increased CO and HC; pollutant effects differ and evidence is limited.

TNO, Analysis of the CO2 emissions of light-duty vehicles, §3.2.5.5, https://climate.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2016-11/analysis_ldv_co2_emissions_en.pdf: gear changes and engine speed affect fuel consumption; eco-driving includes early upshifts to keep engine speed low.

rows.text: A properly matched deflector above the cab directs air over the load and reduces the aerodynamic drag of the combination.
evidence: https://afdc.energy.gov/conserve/equipment, Aerodynamic Equipment: gli airfoil dirigono l’aria sopra la cabina e riducono la resistenza.
https://nepis.epa.gov/Exe/ZyPURL.cgi?Dockey=P1000S9O.TXT, Improved Aerodynamics: deflettori sul tetto tra i dispositivi aerodinamici dei trattori.

rows.text: Drag increases approximately with the square of speed relative to the air, so an increase in speed produces a more than proportional increase in force.
evidence: https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/drag-equation/, equazione D = Cd × ρ × V² × A / 2: area frontale, velocità relativa all’aria e coefficiente determinano la resistenza.

rows.text: With coefficient, density and air-relative speed unchanged, increasing frontal area increases drag force proportionally.
evidence: https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/drag-equation/, equazione D = Cd × ρ × V² × A / 2: area frontale, velocità relativa all’aria e coefficiente determinano la resistenza.

rows.text: A wet road concerns tire contact with the road; aerodynamic drag instead depends on airflow around the vehicle.
evidence: https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/drag-equation/, equazione D = Cd × ρ × V² × A / 2: area frontale, velocità relativa all’aria e coefficiente determinano la resistenza.

rows.text: Speed matters: other conditions being equal, aerodynamic force rises with the square of speed relative to the air.
evidence: https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/drag-equation/, equazione D = Cd × ρ × V² × A / 2: area frontale, velocità relativa all’aria e coefficiente determinano la resistenza.

rows.text: Excess load takes more energy to move the vehicle and can increase fuel consumption and emissions; the effect on individual pollutants depends on conditions.
evidence: US EPA, Vehicle Weight and CO2 Emissions, https://nepis.epa.gov/Exe/ZyPURL.cgi?Dockey=P10191S7.TXT: greater vehicle weight requires more energy and increases CO2 other conditions equal.

US EPA HERO, Huang et al. (2006), https://hero.epa.gov/reference/1639577/: on-road tests of two diesel trucks found higher NOx and fuel-consumption factors with load; individual CO and HC results varied.

rows.text: The drag coefficient describes the effect of shape and airflow; it does not directly depend on vehicle weight.
evidence: https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/drag-coefficient/, definizione di Cd e dipendenza da forma, inclinazione e condizioni del flusso.

rows.text: Overcoming air resistance requires engine energy, so reducing it can improve fuel consumption.
evidence: https://afdc.energy.gov/conserve/equipment, Aerodynamic Equipment: meno resistenza riduce il carico sul motore e migliora il risparmio di carburante.

rows.text: The relationship is direct, not inverse: other conditions being equal, a larger frontal area produces more drag.
evidence: https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/drag-equation/, equazione D = Cd × ρ × V² × A / 2: area frontale, velocità relativa all’aria e coefficiente determinano la resistenza.

rows.text: Aerodynamic force depends on air-relative speed, area, density and coefficient; it is not directly proportional to maximum engine power.
evidence: https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/drag-equation/, equazione D = Cd × ρ × V² × A / 2: area frontale, velocità relativa all’aria e coefficiente determinano la resistenza.

rows.text: Other conditions being equal, drag force rises with the square of speed relative to the air: doubling that speed quadruples the force.
evidence: https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/drag-equation/, equazione D = Cd × ρ × V² × A / 2: area frontale, velocità relativa all’aria e coefficiente determinano la resistenza.

rows.text: Aerodynamic force is not directly proportional to weight: it depends instead on area, shape, air and relative speed.
evidence: https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/drag-equation/, equazione D = Cd × ρ × V² × A / 2: area frontale, velocità relativa all’aria e coefficiente determinano la resistenza.

issues.reason: The printed VERO asserts coincidence of the rpm near maximum torque with maximum efficiency for internal-combustion engines without specifying engine, load or efficiency measure. Accessible sources support favorable efficiency in some regions, but do not establish that coincidence generally; engine efficiency varies with both speed and load. Independent source adjudication is needed before supplying the claimed maximum.

TNO, 02.OR.VM.004.1/HVDB (2002), appendix A.3/4, https://publications.tno.nl/publication/34613582/N0rnml/02.OR.VM.004.1-HVDB.pdf: typical petrol and diesel maps show brake-specific fuel consumption varying with speed and load, with a minimum region at intermediate speed and high load.

US Department of Energy, Co-Optima webinar, https://www.energy.gov/cmei/fuels/text-version-co-optima-webinar-how-can-co-optimized-fuels-and-spark-ignition-engines: engine efficiency changes substantially with speed and load; some highest efficiencies occur at low speeds and high loads.

The asserted possibility of favourable efficiency near peak-torque rpm needs an inspectable example relating a specific engine efficiency map to its torque peak. The linked TNO PDF exceeds browser fetch limits and the Bosch link returned HTTP 403 in this independent review; provide inspectable copies or alternative primary evidence.

DOE establishes variation with speed and load, while the Volvo brochure describes increased efficiency relative to another engine in 900–1400 rpm, rather than identifying the absolute efficient operating region on a load map. These do not by themselves establish the asserted positive near-peak-torque possibility for an identified operating point. Supply an inspectable model-specific map or equivalent source; retain the qualification and printed verdict.
